subject: QuantumBridge Dedicated commitment: SLO fit & headroom projection
messages:
From: Arielle Stone <arielle.stone@quantumbridge.ai>
To: Ben Carter <ben.carter@redwood.inference>
Date: Fri, 29 Jun 2028 09:12:00 -0700
Subject: Dedicated sizing request and latency targets

Hi Ben —

Thanks again for the demo last week. QuantumBridge is moving toward a production rollout in Q4 and procurement asked for a concrete capacity recommendation from Redwood so we can size the purchase order. High level: our forecasted peak is ~18k active sessions with burst patterns tied to market open windows; average request is ~45 tokens output, median prompt ~200 tokens input (so end-to-end ~245 tokens). Our target SLO is 95th percentile response time <= 300ms for interactive flows.

Key asks:
- Recommended committed GPU slab (H100-equivalent) to meet p95<=300ms for our baseline model family.
- Tokens/sec estimate and headroom buffer (we typically ask for 25–40% safety cushion).
- Burst/overflow strategy and expected fallback latency if capacity is exhausted.

We can share telemetry if helpful — attaching a short traffic pattern CSV (sent in separate email). Can you send a short worksheet with scenarios and an initial priceable commit?

Thanks,
Arielle Stone
Sr. Product Ops, QuantumBridge

From: Ben Carter <ben.carter@redwood.inference>
To: Arielle Stone <arielle.stone@quantumbridge.ai>
Cc: Karthik Iyer <karthik_iyer@redwood.inference>, Priyom Das <priyom_das@redwood.inference>
Date: Sat, 30 Jun 2028 15:20:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Dedicated sizing request and latency targets

Arielle —

Appreciate the traffic sketch. Quick summary up front: attached worksheet (QB-tokens-scenarios-v2.xlsx) has three committed slab options and expected p95 latency projections. High-level recommendation for your forecast and 35% headroom: start with 10 x H100-equivalent reserved nodes + 2-node burst pool. That maps to ~75k tokens/sec sustained for a 13B-class family (FP16), which covers expected peaks with the headroom you asked for; for heavier 70B variants we recommend a mixed slab (6 H100 for 13B + 6 H100 optimized / quantized for larger models) — details in the attachment.

Quick math from our microbenchmarks (detailed in sheet):
- 13B FP16 (seq ~256): ~7,500 tokens/sec per H100-equivalent node in continuous throughput mode.
- 70B quantized 8-bit (seq ~256): ~1,200 tokens/sec per H100-equivalent node.
- Assume median request ~245 tokens -> single-request generation time (p95) maps to tokens/sec and batching. With the 10-node slab above, the 13B path yields p95 ~120–180ms (well under 300ms). The 70B quantized path is closer to 240–320ms at peak — within SLO if you accept the 35% headroom and planned burst.

Operational notes:
- We recommend prefix/KV caching for interactive flows to cut repeat-token cost/latency by ~20–35%.
- Autoscale/burst config: keep 2 hot burst nodes warm; failover policy to compatible quantized variant if primary slab unavailable (fallback adds ~40–70ms).

Next steps:
1) Can we get a short 45-minute runbook review with your infra and procurement teams next week?
2) I’ll share a draft SLA & pricing snapshot once we lock the model mix.

Attaching: QB-tokens-scenarios-v2.xlsx (scenario sheets + microbench assumptions)

—
Ben Carter
Sr. Solutions Engineer | Redwood Inference
ben.carter@redwood.inference
From: Karthik Iyer <karthik_iyer@redwood.inference>
To: Ben Carter <ben.carter@redwood.inference>, Arielle Stone <arielle.stone@quantumbridge.ai>
Cc: Priyom Das <priyom_das@redwood.inference>
Date: Sun, 1 Jul 2028 10:05:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Dedicated sizing request and latency targets

Ben / Arielle —

Adding a technical breakdown so the numbers above have context.

Benchmark assumptions (these are conservative, measured on our H100-equivalent fleet):
- Tokenization: avg token ~4 chars; request composition you sent -> 245 tokens per call on average.
- Effective batching: interactive flows are latency-sensitive; we assume 1.5–2x effective batching at peak due to request coalescing.
- KV/prefix cache hit: 30% on average for your flows (we used that in scenario sheet).

Observed throughput (per H100-eq node):
- 13B FP16, 256 seq: 7,200–7,800 tokens/sec (sustained), p95 per-request 80–180ms depending on batch and token window.
- 33B mixed-precision, 256 seq: 2,800–3,500 tokens/sec, p95 ~150–260ms.
- 70B quantized 8-bit, 256 seq: 1,000–1,400 tokens/sec, p95 ~200–340ms.

Recommendation mapping for QuantumBridge:
- Baseline commit (interactive UI + inference-heavy background): 8 H100-eq nodes focused on 13B family + 4 nodes configured/tainted for larger models (quantized) to support peak analytic/summary workloads. Expected aggregate sustained tokens/sec: ~8*7.5k + 4*1.2k ~= 64k tokens/sec.
- Safety/headroom: add 25–40% buffer depending on burst tolerance. With a 35% buffer, target commit becomes ~86k tokens/sec equivalent — we mapped that to a 10+2 slab in Ben's sheet.

Fallback behaviour: if committed slab is saturated we route new requests to hosted fallback with controlled throttling (best-effort latency 300–600ms) and a degrade-to-shorter-output policy (reduce max tokens by 30%) to protect p95.

Operational asks from QB side for accurate sizing:
- 7 days of per-minute request telemetry (auth/anonymized) so we can fit burst windows precisely.
- Call pattern classification (interactive vs batch) — we used a 60/40 split in the workbook.

Happy to run a short synthetic replay for you using your sample 24-hour trace once we have the telemetry.

—
Karthik Iyer
Principal Performance Engineer | Redwood Inference
From: Arielle Stone <arielle.stone@quantumbridge.ai>
To: Ben Carter <ben.carter@redwood.inference>

Subject: Re: Dedicated sizing request and latency targets

Ben / Karthik —

This is very helpful, thanks. Procurement is happy to see a concrete slab recommendation and the headroom assumptions. Two quick asks before we proceed to a PO:
1) Can you run the 24-hour synthetic replay against the proposed 10+2 slab and share a short p95 latency runbook (one-pager) showing where the p95 sits during market open spikes?
2) Can you include a minor SLA carve (p95 <= 350ms for the first 3 months while we warm caches) in the draft SLA so procurement can recommend initial acceptance?

We’ll prepare the telemetry export and loop back with a calendar invite for next Wednesday (we prefer 10–11am PST). If that test looks good I’ll ask procurement to start the DocuSign flow on the draft SLA you shared.

Thanks,
Arielle
